conviction_note: Nothing decisive found: the only sizeable item is a financing risk inferred from pattern (a $650m raise came with last year's Q3 print, cash falls ~$215m a quarter, and Boeing's $55m forward purchase is conditioned on an Archer offering of at least $400m before March 2027), set against a short book that rose from 90m to 115m shares into the print, a peer (Joby) that rose on its own Q3, and a likely small revenue beat on a stale consensus; p_up 47 on an abs move of 11 gives -0.66, close to the findings' sum of -0.4.
bar: Revenue consensus about $3.6-4.0m (Benzinga $3.7m via search summary; Chartmill $3.64m, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/ACHR/estimates; finviz preview 2026-11-02 says $4.0m, https://finviz.com/news/413699/archers-third-quarter-tests-whether-the-boeing-pivot-can-outrun-a-170-million-quarterly-burn). EPS consensus disputed: -$0.25 (finviz), -$0.27 (Benzinga), -$0.33 (Chartmill). The company's own guide is Q3 adjusted EBITDA loss of $170-200m (Q2 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001824502/000182450226000056/archerq226earningspressr.htm). The stock trades on burn, cash, certification milestones and financing, not on revenue. Because the EPS bar disagrees across sources, every finding is capped small. print_vs_bar_pct is on revenue: Q2 was $5.0m with the Hawthorne FBO already owned for the full quarter, against a ~$3.8m bar.
positioning_check: Short interest 114.8m shares at the 2026-10-15 FINRA settlement, 14.9% of 770m shares outstanding (not float, so the share of float is higher), 4.32 days to cover. It has risen every settlement since 89.9m on 2026-08-14 (91.997m 08-31, 94.4m 09-15, 104.0m 09-30), and Equibles' model puts 10-30 at about 113m (https://equibles.com/stocks/achr/shortinterest, read 2026-11-09). Options (sealed baseline): event-implied move 10.38%, straddle 12.49%, 25-delta skew +6.22 vol points (downside paid), put/call open interest 0.33 (call-heavy). Tape: +12.35% over 5 days, -0.11% over 20 days, 48% below the 52-week high, 23% above the 52-week low; the finviz preview of 2026-11-02 put the stock at $4.20 against a post-earnings low of $3.68 and a 200-day moving average of $5.83. This is a moderately crowded and rising short going into the print, with retail calls on the other side.

findings.finding: Financing risk at or around the print: cash, equivalents and short-term investments fell $215.3m in Q2 to $1,560.6m ($156.4m operating cash use, $37.1m capex, $25m Hawthorne FBO), so Q3 should end near $1.35bn. Archer paired last year's Q3 print (2025-11-06, -7.88% close to close) with a $650m registered direct at $8.00. The Boeing deal's Forward Equity Purchase Agreement lets Archer sell Boeing up to $55m of stock only alongside an Archer equity offering grossing at least $400m, at the lowest price in that offering, with the election due by the later of 2027-03-31 or three months after closing. So a $400m-plus raise is contemplated in the deal documents. No raise has been announced; the stock is $4.69.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-11-06: Q3 2025 print with the $650m raise at $8.00, -7.88% close to close (baseline); the raise headline was reported as -12% intraday (https://www.panabee.com/news/archer-aviation-fortifies-balance-sheet-with-650-million-raise-acquires-la-operational-h). The June 2025 $850m raise at $10.00 was not on a print.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews cite $1.6bn of liquidity and 'about two years' of runway (TIKR, 2026-11-07) and frame dilution as a vague worry; none ties it to the Boeing forward purchase's $400m trigger or to last year's print-day raise. If a print-day raise were priced, the 5-day run-up would not be +12% into the event, and put/call open interest would not be 0.33. The +6.2 skew does lean this way, which partly prices it. What the money buys: burn of about $190m a quarter on a pre-certification aircraft, with no revenue ramp to show for it (revenue is $5m a quarter), so it is not funding demand; but there is no going-concern flag and the runway is more than 12 months, so it is not distress either.
findings.independence: TIKR (https://www.tikr.com/blog/archer-aviation-is-down-45-in-2026-dead-money-or-due-for-a-bounce, updated 2026-11-07) says investors expect more stock sales. The August 424B7 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001824502/000110465926098338/tm2623448-2_424b7.htm) registers 8.26m shares issued to vendors instead of cash, which conserves cash at the cost of dilution. Both are inference about a raise, not a document announcing one.

findings.finding: The piloted transition flight has still not been publicly confirmed. On the Q2 call (Aug 2026) management said Archer is 'on track to full transition later this year' and is 'actively working with the FAA on for-credit testing this year'; in June 2026 Simply Wall St and in August 2026 Flying Magazine both noted Midnight had not yet flown a piloted transition. No release through 2026-11-09 announces one, despite the No Roads Tour flights. Meanwhile Joby reported a 'wide range of for-credit testing' in the final FAA stage on 2026-11-04. The Q3 update will either announce the milestone (positive) or repeat or slip the 'later this year' timing, with seven weeks of the year left.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-03-02 Q4 2025 print, -10.64%, and 2025-02-11, -8.92%, both on prints read as timeline-heavy (cause not verified line by line). 2025-05-12, +22.91%, came on a print with the LA28 deal and milestones. Milestone news has moved this name by double digits on prints in both directions.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews (finviz 2026-11-02) list 'more than 150 piloted test flights' and Phase 4 progress but do not flag that the piloted transition promised for 2026 is still unannounced. If the market expected a slip, the skew would be wider than +6 and calls would not dominate open interest. The sign is genuinely uncertain because Archer could announce the milestone with the print, so the size is small and the band symmetric.
findings.independence: https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/capital-goods/nyse-achr/archer-aviation/news/archers-missing-transition-flight-keeps-focus-on-certificati (2026-06-05) and Flying Magazine via search (2026-08-04) record the missing flight. Joby's for-credit progress: https://www.jobyaviation.com/news/joby-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results (2026-11-04).

findings.finding: Revenue should come in at or above Q2's $5.0m, against a stale consensus of $3.6-4.0m. Q2 was $3.0m FBO, $1.0m lease and $1.0m other, and the Hawthorne FBO controlling stake closed 2026-04-01, so Q2 already held a full quarter of FBO revenue; nothing in the filings points to Q3 losing it. That is a revenue beat of about 20-35%, on a line the stock does not trade on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue $5.0m against a $1.95m consensus (about 2.5x) and the stock rose +8.47%, but that print also announced the Boeing/Wisk/Insitu deal, so the revenue beat cannot be isolated. The stock then fell about 33% over the next three months.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus implies a sequential slide from $5.0m to $3.6-4.0m (finviz 2026-11-02 notes the implied slip), which is what it would not show if the street had modelled the full-quarter FBO. The amounts are trivial against a $170-200m quarterly loss, so even when it lands it is worth very little.
findings.independence: Revenue consensus from https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/ACHR/estimates and https://finviz.com/news/413699/archers-third-quarter-tests-whether-the-boeing-pivot-can-outrun-a-170-million-quarterly-burn; the FBO timing is from the 10-Q only.

findings.finding: Adjusted EBITDA loss is likely to land inside the $170-200m guide again and near its low end: Q1 was $172.5m and Q2 $177.1m against the same range, and on the Q2 call the CFO said the loss would 'stay within the same range' and that cash burn would stay 'relatively flat' after the Boeing assets are folded in.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 and Q2 2026 both landed near the low end of the same range; the reactions were -2.29% and +8.47%, so the burn line alone has not moved the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it lands inside a guide the company gave, so it is a reported-quarter item the market was told to expect. The residual is the Q4 guide; the preview (finviz 2026-11-02) flags a widening as the risk, and holding the range would be a small positive.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2 call with finding 2 (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/17/archer-aviation-achr-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/).

findings.finding: Peer read: Joby reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-04 (revenue $55m, full-year revenue guide raised to $135-140m from $115-125m, $2.2bn cash, no raise) and rose 5.0% the next session while the S&P 500 fell about 4.4% on an AI-led selloff. That is the sector's most recent counterparty print and it was bought. ACHR has risen 12.35% over 5 days into its own print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured ACHR-on-Joby print relationship in the baseline. TIKR notes both names fell together in the 2026-10-22 Nasdaq selloff.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced already: ACHR's +12% five-day run-up is probably in part this sympathy, which also raises the risk that the stock sells the news. Archer has no revenue guide to raise in the way Joby (Blade) did, so the transmission is weak. This is a proxy and is sized as one.
findings.independence: Joby release https://www.jobyaviation.com/news/joby-reports-third-quarter-2026-financial-results (2026-11-04); market drop from https://www.lanacion.com.ar/usa/how-major-us-stock-indexes-fared-thursday-1152026-nid05112026/ (sources disagree on the exact percentage).

findings.finding: The Boeing deal is moving toward closing: the HSR waiting period expired 2026-09-18 (8-K 2026-09-24), other regulatory approvals are 'underway', and the company still targets year-end 2026. The deal brings Insitu, which management says has more than $200m of annual revenue and is expected to be free-cash-flow positive. The print may firm the closing date or give the first combined financial outline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The deal announcement on the Q2 print coincided with +8.47%; TIKR says rallies on the Thunder reveal and on the Boeing deal 'each lasted only a day'.
findings.why_not_priced: The HSR expiry is public and priced. What is not is any combined-company outlook (Insitu's revenue against 2026 consensus of $15.1m and 2027 of $138m per TIKR); if consensus already held Insitu at full run rate, a closing confirmation would add nothing. Sized small because nothing says the print carries a pro forma outlook.
findings.independence: Same deal as finding 7; Insitu figures from the Q2 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/17/archer-aviation-achr-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/).

findings.finding: The Boeing purchase agreement gives Boeing a termination right 'if the Company's enterprise value (as calculated in accordance with the Purchase Agreement) is below a minimum level for a specified period'. The threshold is not disclosed in the 8-K summary, and the stock is about 33% below where it traded after the deal was announced. Any disclosure on the call that the condition is close, or any hedging language about closing, would be a negative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None; this has never been tested.
findings.why_not_priced: No preview mentions the clause. Without the threshold (it sits in Exhibit 2.1, not read) it cannot be said whether $4.69 is anywhere near it, so this is an inference and is sized at almost nothing. If the market were worried about it, the September HSR news would not have been read as closing on track.
findings.independence: None. The 2026-09-24 8-K still says year-end closing is expected.

findings.finding: Short interest rose from 89.9m shares (2026-08-14) to 114.8m (2026-10-15, 14.9% of shares outstanding, 4.3 days to cover) into the print, while put/call open interest is 0.33. A print without a raise and with milestones held leaves a growing short to cover against call-heavy retail positioning; the +12% five-day move may already be part of that covering.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two largest up-moves in the baseline (+22.91% 2025-05-12, +12.12% 2025-02-27) came on prints without a raise; the print-day raise of 2025-11-06 was -7.88%.
findings.why_not_priced: The +6.22 put skew says the option market is paying for downside; this finding is the mechanism on the other side. Its sign depends on finding 1 (no raise), so the two are not independent, and it is sized small.
findings.independence: The baseline's put/call OI of 0.33 and 5-day run-up of +12.35% are from a different source (Yahoo options and bars). Days to cover of 4.1 at 09-30 are confirmed by https://massive.com/quote/achr (read 2026-10-26).

findings.finding: Sell-side targets have been cut into the print: Goldman kept Neutral and cut its target to $7 from $8 (mid-October), Barclays upgraded with an $8 target in October, and the mean target fell from $12.44 to $10.89 over the year while the lowest target rose to $7 from $4.50. Every target is above the $4.69 spot.
findings.why_not_priced: It is wire copy and priced; filed for completeness at zero.

outside_window.finding: Boeing/Wisk/Insitu/SkyGrid closing targeted by end of 2026 (outside date 2027-05-09); a special meeting within 60 days after closing is needed for warrant and forward-purchase approvals.

Joby v. Archer trade-secret case: on 2026-09-29 the court narrowed Joby's claims, let others proceed, and dismissed Archer's Lanham Act and UCL counterclaims without leave to amend. There is no dated ruling inside the window.

baseline_tension: The small net negative agrees with the +6.22 put skew, so it is probably partly priced, and it cuts against the +12% five-day run-up, the call-heavy open interest and a short book that rose about 28% since August. That leaves p_up only 3 points below 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 4 (financing is a question): I asked what a raise would buy. It funds pre-certification burn with no corroborated revenue ramp, but there is no going-concern flag and the runway is about 6-7 quarters, so it is a negative but not distress. Together with rule 5 (an inference, not an announced raise) and rule 7 (a rising, moderately crowded short), the financing finding went from -1.5 to -1.2.

Rule 6 (bar unsourced or disputed): EPS consensus disagrees across three sources (-0.25 / -0.27 / -0.33), so every finding stays capped small; the revenue finding went from +0.3 to +0.2, also under rule 1 (revenue is not the line this stock trades on).

Rule 5 (proxy and inference smaller): the transition-flight finding (an inference from an absent announcement) went from -0.5 to -0.4, and the EV-termination clause with an unknown threshold went from -0.3 to -0.2.
Rule 6 (inside the guide): the burn finding stays at +0.2, already sized as a reported-quarter item inside the company's guide.
Rule 7 (skew and short interest): checked; the net negative sign agrees with the skew, and the positioning finding keeps +0.5. abs_move_pct (11) and p_up (47) unchanged.
